newsitem.title: FRANCE: Scor share offer heavily oversubscribed.
newsitem.headline: Scor share offer heavily oversubscribed.

text.p: French reinsurer Scor said on Thursday that Union des Assurance de Paris's offering of seven million Scor shares via a placement in the United States and Europe was oversubscribed more than four times.
This, it said, led UAP to raise its offering to eight million shares in response to strong demand for the stock.
UAP has also given the underwriters a greenshoe option to purchase up to an additional 1.2 million Scor shares solely to cover oversubscription.
The shares will henceforth be listed on the Paris bourse and the New York Stock Exchange, ticker "SCO", Scor said in a statement.
The share offer was timed to coincide with Scor's plans to debut on Wall Street.
"This success marks the final stage in the modification of Scor's share ownership announced by chairman Jacques Blondeau at the beginning of the year," Scor said in a statement.
"Scor now has an international shareholder base, made up of a number of important institutional investors and investment funds which are mainly European but also American."

UAP, which originally held 40.9 percent of Scor, said in a separate statement it sold its Scor shares at a price of 197 francs per share. Its original plans to sell seven million shares represented 26 percent of Scor's capital.
UAP said some 1.4 billion francs in proceeds from the sale would be used to reduce its debt and the remainder would be used for continuing the restructuring of its insurance assets.
UAP said it planned to keep its remaining Scor shares over the long term.

Scor said a substantial float had been created that would "ensure active trading in the shares. It has also brought together a group of long-term investors which, together with UAP, will hold some 20 percent of the capital stock."
Scor said the membership of its board of directors would be changed soon to reflect the new make-up of the share ownership.
